title: Rotate a List to the Right

concept.title: Close the list into a ring, then cut it at the right place
body: Rotating a list to the right by `k` places moves the last `k` nodes to the front. A short way: find the **length** `n` and the **tail**; connect the tail to the head (a ring); walk to the new tail, which is the node at index `n - k - 1`; its successor is the new head; cut the ring there.

body.code:
k %= length                       # rotating by the length changes nothing
if k == 0: return head
new_tail = head
for _ in range(length - k - 1):
    new_tail = new_tail.next
new_head = new_tail.next
new_tail.next = None              # cut the ring
tail.next = head                  # old tail now points to the old head
return new_head

body: Always reduce `k` with `k % length` first: `k` can be huge (here up to 10^9), and rotating by a multiple of the length gives the same list. Do not forget the lists with one node or none.

statement: Rotate a singly linked list to the right by `k` places (the last `k` nodes move to the front, in the same order) and print the result.
inputFormat: The second line has the values of the nodes, from the head to the tail.
outputFormat: Print the values of the rotated list on one line.

examples.note: The last two nodes move to the front: 4 5 1 2 3.

hints: Find the length and the tail node in one walk.
Replace `k` by `k % length`; if it is 0 the list does not change.
The new tail is the node at index `length - k - 1`. Cut after it and link the old tail to the old head.

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

# Every node is also remembered in this list. Python in the browser cannot free a very long chain of nodes at once,
# so free_nodes() (called at the end) cuts the links first and the nodes are then freed one by one.
all_nodes = []


class ListNode:
    def __init__(self, val, next=None):
        self.val = val
        self.next = next
        all_nodes.append(self)


def free_nodes():
    for node in all_nodes:
        node.next = None
        if hasattr(node, "random"):
            node.random = None
    all_nodes.clear()


# Builds a list from the values. If pos is 0 or more, the last node points back to the node at index pos (a cycle).
def build_list(values, pos=-1):
    head = None
    for v in reversed(values):
        head = ListNode(v, head)
    if pos >= 0:
        tail = head
        while tail.next is not None:
            tail = tail.next
        target = head
        for _ in range(pos):
            target = target.next
        tail.next = target
    return head


# Prints the values of a list on one line ("empty" for an empty list).
def print_list(head):
    out = []
    while head is not None:
        out.append(head.val)
        head = head.next
    print(*(out if out else ["empty"]))


def rotate_right(head, k):
    if head is None or head.next is None:
        return head
    length = 1
    tail = head
    while tail.next is not None:
        tail = tail.next
        length += 1
    k %= length
    if k == 0:
        return head
    new_tail = head
    for _ in range(length - k - 1):
        new_tail = new_tail.next
    new_head = new_tail.next
    new_tail.next = None
    tail.next = head
    return new_head

n, k = map(int, input().split())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))

print_list(rotate_right(build_list(a), k))
free_nodes()
